tools.name: trowel
tools.for: spreading mortar, and tapping bricks down to the line
tools.hold: Hold the handle in your fist, thumb on top, the blade low and flat.
tools.safety: Gloves on: wet mortar is rough on skin.

tools.name: spirit level
tools.for: checking that a row is level and a wall is straight up
tools.hold: Lay it along the bricks and keep it still, then read the bubble.
tools.safety: Carry it by the middle, so its ends never swing into anyone.

tools.name: plumb line
tools.for: checking that a wall is straight up and down
tools.hold: Hold the string at the top of the wall and let the weight hang still.
tools.safety: Let the weight hang: never swing it.

tools.name: tape measure
tools.for: measuring how long, wide or high something is
tools.hold: Hook the end on the start, then pull the tape straight to the end.
tools.safety: Let the tape roll back slowly: its edge can nip fingers.

tools.name: builder's square
tools.for: checking that a corner is square (a right angle)
tools.hold: Put it right in the corner, one arm along each wall.
tools.safety: Lay it down flat when you are not using it.

tools.name: claw hammer
tools.for: driving nails in, and pulling them out with the claw
tools.hold: Hold it near the end of the handle and start with little taps.
tools.safety: Goggles on; let go of the nail once it stands up by itself.

tools.name: handsaw
tools.for: cutting wood to length
tools.hold: One hand on the handle, first finger pointing along it: long, slow strokes.
tools.safety: Goggles on, the wood held tight, your other hand well away from the teeth.

tools.name: shovel
tools.for: moving sand and gravel, and tipping them where they go
tools.hold: One hand near the blade, one on the handle; bend your knees, not your back.
tools.safety: Lift small loads, and never swing it near anyone.

tools.name: bucket
tools.for: carrying and pouring water
tools.hold: One hand on the handle, the other under the bottom to tip it.
tools.safety: Half full is easier to carry, and there are no spills to slip on.

tools.name: paint roller
tools.for: painting walls quickly and evenly
tools.hold: Roll it in the tray, then up and down the wall in long strokes.
tools.safety: Open a window: fresh air while you paint.

tools.name: sandpaper
tools.for: making wood smooth
tools.hold: Wrap it round a block and rub along the grain.
tools.safety: A dust mask on, and sweep the dust up after.

tools.name: cement mixer
tools.for: mixing sand, cement and water into mortar
tools.hold: A grown-up runs it; you tell them the order.
tools.safety: Gloves and goggles on; never hands or a shovel inside while it turns.

order.words: more water, until it is like soft butter
switch it off before it is tipped out

safety.words: gloves on: wet cement burns skin
goggles on: cement dust hurts eyes
never hands or a shovel inside while it turns

tools.name: drill
tools.for: making holes and driving screws
tools.hold: Both hands, pressing straight in; squeeze the trigger gently.
tools.safety: Goggles on; the battery out to change the bit.

order.words: the bit tight in the chuck

safety.words: the battery out to change the bit

tools.name: hard hat
tools.for: protecting your head on a building site
tools.hold: Straight on your head, the strap done up.
tools.safety: On a building site it stays on, all the time.

tools.name: safety goggles
tools.for: keeping dust and chips out of your eyes
tools.hold: Over your eyes, the strap snug round your head.
tools.safety: Goggles on before you saw, drill or hammer.

tools.name: gloves
tools.for: keeping hands safe and clean: work gloves for building, thin gloves for first aid
tools.hold: Pull them all the way on, one finger in each.
tools.safety: Thin first aid gloves are used once, then thrown away.

tools.name: screwdriver
tools.for: turning screws in and out
tools.hold: Push straight in while you turn: righty-tighty, lefty-loosey.
tools.safety: Use the right size tip, and never turn towards your other hand.

tools.name: spanner
tools.for: turning nuts and bolts
tools.hold: Fit it snugly on the nut and pull the handle round.
tools.safety: Pull towards you rather than push, so a slip can't bump your knuckles.

tools.name: pliers
tools.for: gripping, bending and holding small things
tools.hold: Handles in your palm; squeeze to grip.
tools.safety: Keep fingers out of the jaws.

tools.name: Allen key
tools.for: the six-sided screws of flat-pack furniture
tools.hold: The short end in the screw; turn it with the long end.
tools.safety: Push it all the way in so it doesn't slip.

tools.name: glue gun
tools.for: sticking things together with hot glue
tools.hold: Squeeze the trigger gently, the hot tip pointing down.
tools.safety: The tip and the glue are hot: a grown-up nearby, and the stand under it.

tools.name: child-safe knife
tools.for: cutting food safely
tools.hold: The claw grip: fingertips tucked in, the knife slicing beside your knuckles.
tools.safety: Cut on a board, away from you, with a grown-up nearby.

tools.name: measuring jug
tools.for: measuring and pouring liquids
tools.hold: Hold it level at eye height to read the line, then pour slowly.
tools.safety: Wipe up spills so nobody slips.

tools.name: whisk
tools.for: mixing, and beating air into eggs and cream
tools.hold: Hold the bowl with your other hand; quick strokes back and forth.
tools.safety: Keep it in the bowl while it moves.

tools.name: kitchen scales
tools.for: weighing food for a recipe
tools.hold: Bowl on first, press zero, then spoon the food in slowly.
tools.safety: Keep them dry and away from the hob.

tools.name: kettle
tools.for: boiling water
tools.hold: Fill it to the line, switch it on, and let a grown-up pour.
tools.safety: Steam and boiling water burn: switch it off and let a grown-up pour.

order.words: dry hands, the cable tucked away
fill it to the line, not past it
wait: it clicks off by itself
a grown-up pours, slowly, away from you

safety.words: dry hands, the cable tucked away
steam and boiling water burn: a grown-up pours

tools.name: microwave
tools.for: warming food
tools.hold: Door, food in, door shut, the time, start.
tools.safety: Never metal or foil inside; hot bowls need oven gloves.

order.words: the food in a microwave-safe bowl
oven gloves on to take it out

safety.words: no metal or foil inside: it sparks

tools.name: tap
tools.for: turning water on and off
tools.hold: Turn it anticlockwise to open and clockwise to close.
tools.safety: Feel the water first: hot taps can scald.

tools.name: broom
tools.for: sweeping the floor
tools.hold: Hands apart on the handle; short sweeps towards a pile.
tools.safety: Lean it against a wall when you stop, so nobody trips.

tools.name: washing machine
tools.for: washing clothes
tools.hold: Sort, load, powder, programme, start.
tools.safety: Never climb in or play with the door; a grown-up chooses the programme.

order.words: load the drum, close the door

safety.words: never climb in or play with the door

tools.name: watering can
tools.for: watering plants
tools.hold: One hand on the top handle, one on the back; tip it gently at the roots.
tools.safety: Fill it half way: lighter to carry.

tools.name: spade
tools.for: digging
tools.hold: Push it in with your foot, then lever the soil up.
tools.safety: Shoes on, never sandals, and feet clear of the blade.

tools.name: secateurs
tools.for: cutting stems and small branches
tools.hold: Squeeze the handles, the thin blade towards the plant.
tools.safety: Close them after use, with a grown-up nearby.

tools.name: rake
tools.for: gathering leaves and making soil flat
tools.hold: Hands apart on the handle; pull it towards you.
tools.safety: Lay it down teeth first so nobody steps on them.

tools.name: clean cloth
tools.for: pressing on a cut to stop it bleeding
tools.hold: Fold it into a pad and press firmly on the cut.
tools.safety: Gloves on if you can, and tell a grown-up.

tools.name: plaster
tools.for: covering a small cut
tools.hold: Peel the backing off, stick it on, smooth the edges down.
tools.safety: Wash the cut clean first, with a grown-up.

tools.name: cling film
tools.for: covering a cooled burn
tools.hold: Lay it loosely over the burn: never wrap it tight.
tools.safety: Cool the burn under running water for 20 minutes first.

tools.name: fire extinguisher
tools.for: putting out a small fire
tools.hold: Pull, aim, squeeze, sweep.
tools.safety: A grown-up uses it on a small fire with the way out behind; if in doubt, get out.

order: aim at the bottom of the fire

tools.name: smoke alarm
tools.for: warning everyone early when there is smoke
tools.hold: A grown-up presses and holds the test button until it beeps.
tools.safety: Test it every month, and never take its battery out.

order.words: press and hold the test button

safety.words: a grown-up tests it once a month

tools.name: coins
tools.for: paying, and giving change
tools.hold: Count them out one by one, the biggest first.
tools.safety: Keep money safe, and never give it to a stranger who asks.

tools.name: shop till
tools.for: adding up and taking payment in a shop
tools.hold: Each price in, then press PAY.
tools.safety: Check the total before you pay.

order: the needs on the list first
wants only if there is room

tools.name: card reader
tools.for: paying by card (pretend in the game: never a real PIN)
tools.hold: Check the price, tap the card, cover the keys, type the PIN, press OK.
tools.safety: A PIN is secret: never tell it to anyone, ever.

order.words: check the price on the screen
tap or put in the card
cover the keys with your other hand

safety.words: cover the keys: a PIN is secret, always
in the game it is pretend: never a real PIN

tools.name: ledger
tools.for: writing down money in and money out, to see the profit (My Business's shop)
tools.hold: Write each sale in and each cost out straight away, then take money out from money in.
tools.safety: Check the sums twice: a mistake in the ledger hides a loss.

shows: money in, money out and profit
order: money in take away money out is the profit

tools.name: price board
tools.for: reading a market's prices today, and why they moved (the Market Square)
tools.hold: Find the good, read its price and its arrow, then read why it moved.
tools.safety: Prices change with the seasons: read today's before you buy or sell.

safety: a fair price is honest for both sides

tools.name: phone
tools.for: calling, and calling for help in an emergency
tools.hold: Press the numbers, press call, speak slowly and clearly.
tools.safety: Emergency numbers are only for a real emergency.

safety: emergency numbers only for a real emergency
never type your address or number into a game

tools.name: keyboard
tools.for: typing letters and numbers
tools.hold: Fingers resting on the middle row; press each key lightly.
tools.safety: Never type your address, phone number or passwords into a game or a chat.

tools.name: camera
tools.for: taking pictures
tools.hold: Two hands, elbows in; hold still, then press.
tools.safety: Ask before you take a picture of a person.

tools.name: ruler
tools.for: measuring short lengths
tools.hold: Line the 0 up with the start, then read where the end is.
tools.safety: Rulers are for measuring, not for flicking.

tools.name: thermometer
tools.for: measuring how hot or cold something is
tools.hold: Hold it still in the thing you measure until the number stops changing.
tools.safety: Clean it after use, and never put a lab thermometer in your mouth.

tools.name: magnifying glass
tools.for: making small things look bigger
tools.hold: Hold it near the thing, then move your eye until it is clear.
tools.safety: Never look at the Sun through it, and never leave it in sunlight.

tools.name: stopwatch
tools.for: timing things
tools.hold: Press start, and press again to stop.
tools.safety: Keep it on its strap when you run.

tools.name: bike pump
tools.for: filling tyres with air
tools.hold: Fix it on the valve, hold it steady, push the handle all the way down.
tools.safety: Stop when the tyre feels firm: too much air can burst it.

tools.name: bike helmet
tools.for: protecting your head on a bike or a scooter
tools.hold: Two fingers above your eyebrows, the straps in a V under your ears, snug under the chin.
tools.safety: On every ride, even short ones.

tools.name: compass
tools.for: finding north
tools.hold: Hold it flat and still, then turn until the needle sits on N.
tools.safety: Keep it away from magnets and phones: they pull the needle.

tools.name: scissors
tools.for: cutting paper and card
tools.hold: Thumb in the small hole, fingers in the big one; cut away from you.
tools.safety: Walk with them closed, points down.

tools.name: paintbrush
tools.for: painting
tools.hold: Hold it like a pencil, a little further up; smooth strokes.
tools.safety: Wash it out when you finish.

tools.name: mallet
tools.for: playing a xylophone or a drum
tools.hold: Hold it loosely and let it bounce off the bar.
tools.safety: Gentle taps: the sound is in the bounce.

tools.name: glue stick
tools.for: sticking paper
tools.hold: Twist a little up, then rub it over the back of the paper.
tools.safety: Put the lid back on.

tools.name: soap
tools.for: washing germs off your hands
tools.hold: Press the pump once, then rub palms, backs, between the fingers and thumbs for 20 seconds.
tools.safety: Rinse it all off, and keep it out of your eyes.

tools.name: towel
tools.for: drying clean hands
tools.hold: Rub your hands dry, fronts and backs.
tools.safety: A clean, dry towel: damp ones spread germs.

tools.name: spoon
tools.for: stirring, and spooning food onto the scales
tools.hold: Hold the handle like a pencil and stir slowly round the bowl.
tools.safety: A wooden spoon in a hot pan: metal ones get hot.

tools.name: oven gloves
tools.for: holding hot trays and dishes
tools.hold: Both hands in the gloves, grip the tray's sides firmly.
tools.safety: Dry gloves only: wet ones let the heat through.

tools.name: torch
tools.for: seeing, and being seen, in the dark
tools.hold: Press the switch and point it at the ground ahead.
tools.safety: Never shine it into someone's eyes.

tools.name: hob
tools.for: cooking in a pan
tools.hold: Cook on it with a grown-up: the pan on the ring, its handle turned in.
tools.safety: The rings stay hot after they are off: never touch them.

safety: handles in, away from the edge
tea towels and sleeves away from the rings

tools.name: oven
tools.for: baking and roasting
tools.hold: Oven gloves on, step back from the hot air, then take the tray out.
tools.safety: A grown-up near; the door, the racks and the trays are all hot.

order: open the door and step back
put it on a heat mat
safety: the hot air when the door opens

tools.name: tablet
tools.for: reading, learning and talking to friends
tools.hold: Hold it with both hands and tap gently with one finger.
tools.safety: Never share your name, school or photos with strangers; tell a grown-up if something feels wrong.

order: if it is unkind: block and report

tools.name: seat belt
tools.for: keeping you safe in a car
tools.hold: Pull it across, low over your hips and over your shoulder, and click it in.
tools.safety: On for every trip, in a booster seat while you are small.

order: sit in your seat (a booster seat for children)
safety: low on the hips, never across the neck

tools.name: pedestrian crossing
tools.for: crossing a busy road safely
tools.hold: Press the button on the pole, then wait for the green man.
tools.safety: Look and listen again before you step out, even on green.

tools.name: car
tools.for: getting around by road
tools.hold: A grown-up drives; here you learn the pedals and the rules.
tools.safety: Seat belts on for everyone, and never distract the driver.

tools.name: life jacket
tools.for: keeping you floating in the water
tools.hold: Zip it and click every buckle. Lifted at the shoulders, it stays down, never up past your chin.
tools.safety: On in every boat and by open water, the right size for your weight.

tools.name: float (lifebuoy)
tools.for: throwing to someone in the water, so you never go in
tools.hold: Hold the rope's end, throw it underarm just past them, then pull them in slowly.
tools.safety: Stay back from the edge, low and steady: never go in after them.

tools.name: reaching pole
tools.for: reaching someone in the water from the side or the bank (a long branch works too)
tools.hold: Lie or kneel, hold it out to them, keep it still while they grab it, then pull slowly.
tools.safety: Stay low and back from the edge so you can't be pulled in.

tools.name: whistle
tools.for: being heard far away when you need help
tools.hold: Blow it again and again: it carries much further than a voice.
tools.safety: Keep one on your coat or bag when you walk in the hills or the woods.

tools.name: emergency bag
tools.for: having what your family needs ready in an emergency
tools.hold: Water, food that keeps, a torch, a whistle, first aid and warm layers, ready by the door.
tools.safety: Check it with a grown-up twice a year, and swap old water and food.

tools.name: child lock
tools.for: keeping cleaners and medicines locked away from small children
tools.hold: Close the door and press until it clicks; pull gently to check it holds.
tools.safety: Cleaners and medicines live up high, locked away, put back straight after use.

controls: the latch on the cupboard door
safety: cleaners and medicines live up high, locked away
a grown-up puts them back straight after use

tools.name: carbon monoxide alarm
tools.for: warning you of carbon monoxide, a gas you can't see, smell or taste
tools.hold: A grown-up presses and holds the test button until it beeps, every month.
tools.safety: If it sounds: everyone out into fresh air, and call the emergency number from outside.

order: press and hold the test button
safety: if it sounds for real: everyone out into fresh air
call the emergency number from outside

tools.name: fuse box
tools.for: the home's main switch and safety switches, where all the electricity comes in
tools.hold: Know where it is. A grown-up opens its cover and uses the switches with dry hands.
tools.safety: A grown-up's job. The main switch turns all the power off; never open its insides.

controls: the RCD and its test button
order: the main switch off turns all the power off
safety: dry hands and a dry floor

tools.name: RCD (safety switch)
tools.for: switching the power off fast if electricity goes the wrong way, like through a person
tools.hold: A grown-up presses its test button: it switches off. Then they switch it back on.
tools.safety: Tested as its label says (often every three months); if it won't switch off, call an electrician.

safety: if it doesn't switch off, call an electrician

tools.name: plug
tools.for: connecting a lamp or a machine to a socket
tools.hold: Hold the plug itself to pull it out, never the cable. Dry hands, always.
tools.safety: A cracked plug or a damaged cable: stop using it and tell a grown-up.

tools.name: auto-injector trainer pen
tools.for: practising how an allergy pen works: a trainer has no needle and no medicine
tools.hold: In your fist, orange end down. Blue to the sky, orange to the thigh, until it clicks.
tools.safety: A real pen is only ever the person's own, prescribed for them. Then call the emergency number.

order: hold it in your fist, orange end down
orange to the outer thigh until it clicks
safety: a real pen is only the person's own
a trainer has no needle and no medicine

tools.name: inhaler and spacer
tools.for: breathing in asthma medicine: the spacer helps it reach the lungs
tools.hold: Cap off, shake, into the spacer. Breathe out, press once, then breathe slowly through it.
tools.safety: Only the person's own inhaler, the way their asthma plan says. Not getting better: call for help.

tools.name: pan lid
tools.for: covering a pan, and putting out a small pan fire by keeping the air out
tools.hold: Slide it on from the side, heat off first, and leave it on until the pan is cold.
tools.safety: Never water on a pan fire. A fire that won't go out: get out, stay out, call for help.

tools.name: habit calendar
tools.for: ticking off each day you keep a small habit (the Goal Board)
tools.hold: Choose one small habit, do it, then tick today's square.
tools.safety: No guilt: a missed day never undoes the others. Just carry on tomorrow.

order: a day off: carry on tomorrow
safety: a missed day never undoes the others

tools.name: saving jar
tools.for: saving money a little at a time for a goal
tools.hold: Save first, after each lesson: coins in the slot, count them each week.
tools.safety: Keep real money at home, and count it with a grown-up.

safety: count real money with a grown-up

tools.name: metro ticket
tools.for: going through the metro's gates (Find Your Way)
tools.hold: Hold it flat and tap it on the gate's reader; wait for the green light, then walk through.
tools.safety: One person at a time through the gates; on the platform, stand behind the yellow line.

tools.name: washing label
tools.for: telling you how to wash, dry and iron your clothes: its symbols (Home Helper)
tools.hold: Find it inside the collar or a side seam and read its symbols: the tub's number is the hottest wash in degrees.
tools.safety: A cross over a symbol means no: no hot wash, no tumble dryer, no iron.

tools.name: ticket gates
tools.for: letting people with a ticket through to the metro's platforms (Find Your Way)
tools.hold: Tap your ticket on the reader, wait for the green light, then walk through.
tools.safety: One person at a time; a red cross means ask the staff for help.

controls: the reader where you tap your ticket
shows: a green light and an arrow: go through
a red cross: ask the staff
order: tap your ticket on the reader
walk through, one at a time
safety: on the platform, stand behind the yellow line

tools.name: help point
tools.for: talking to the station's staff when you need help (Find Your Way)
tools.hold: Press the help button, then say what's wrong and which station you're at.
tools.safety: Stay where the staff can find you; it is only for help.

shows: a light while the staff are talking
order: say what's wrong and where you are
safety: stay where the staff can find you

tools.name: dishwasher
tools.for: washing plates, cups and cutlery (Home Helper)
tools.hold: Scrape the plates; plates below, cups upside down on top; sharp knives point down in the basket.
tools.safety: Sharp knives point down; keep its door shut when you're not loading it; a grown-up starts it.

order: plates in the bottom rack, cups on top
close the door; a grown-up starts it
safety: keep the door shut when you're not loading it
